I will not tell you which letter is right for q3. Quiz 0001 is still ungraded, and a retake counts as taking it, so the quiz still has to measure what you can do.

Here are three steps you can take toward the answer on your own:

1. **Analogy.** A soccer team keeps running the same corner-kick routine and the defense keeps clearing it. Someone on the sideline has to decide what to change, because the players on the pitch will keep running the routine. Ask what in an agent plays the sideline role, and what the model can and cannot do about its own repetition. The analogy breaks down because a coach watches from outside the game, while the model sits inside the loop it is in.
2. **Worked example on a different case.** Suppose a script that resizes images slows down and eventually crashes. Three candidate fixes are "buy more RAM", "add a cap on how many images it processes per run" and "wait and see". For each fix, ask two questions. Does it act on the cause of the failure? And if the cause stays, what happens on the next run? Apply the same two questions to every fix and compare what you get.
3. **Check on every option.** For each of a–d, replay step 41 in the quiz scenario. The agent's context still holds all 40 earlier steps, and the failing test is unchanged. Write down what the agent does at step 41 under each option, then ask which option changes the program rather than only the model's inputs. The stem says "change to the agent program", so that phrase is a constraint to apply to all four options.

Which of the four options changes what happens at step 41, and what is your reasoning for each? Once the quiz is graded, I will go through q3 with you in full.
